cards.card_text: This is a psalm of David, written for the choirmaster, to be played with stringed instruments.

cards.verse_text: With stringed instruments, according to Sheminith.

cards.card_text: The note at the top says it's for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments, from when the Ziphites, people from the town of Ziph in Judah (Joshua 15:55), went to Saul, king of Israel (1 Samuel 15:1), and said, “Is David not hiding among us?” I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer and NOBODY came looking for me, but David can't even hide without the neighbors handing out DIRECTIONS!
This is a psalm of David, for the choirmaster, with stringed instruments, and David opens by praying straight to God.
This one's a song of David, Israel's king, written for the choirmaster with stringed instruments.
This one's a song for the choirmaster, played on stringed instruments.
This song is a psalm of Asaph, a song leader in David's day (1 Chronicles 16:5), and it's set for stringed instruments.
He ends with this: "The LORD will save me; we will play songs on stringed instruments all the days of our lives in the house of the LORD." Fifteen more years, and the king is putting a band together.
